prompts.initial_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: one individual full-body 2D fighting-game walking sprite, James Taylor from The House of the Dead 2, contact pose A.
Input image 1: authoritative existing project sprite; use it to preserve the exact character identity, gray suit, white shirt, dark tie, brown swept hair, face, black shoes, black pistol, proportions, shading, colors, fine pixel-edged painted arcade-sprite style and right-facing orientation.
Primary request: change ONLY the walking pose into a cautious forward combat step. Keep the head, torso, arms and two-handed pistol guard closely aligned to the reference. The near-camera leg steps FORWARD toward screen right, its heel contacting the ground; the far leg extends backward toward screen left with its heel lifted and toe touching the same ground line. Clearly readable, natural opposite legs, neither a static wide guard nor a running leap. No body rotation or mirrored character.
Composition: exactly 1024 x 1024 square canvas; one character only, full body fully inside the image. Torso center around x=512. Maintain reference head height near y=60, ground/lowest sole y=960. Preserve approximately the reference scale and generous clear padding. The character looks and aims toward screen right.
Scene/backdrop: true transparent RGBA background, alpha zero outside the sprite, no background color, no checkerboard, no floor, no cast shadow.
Constraints: one pose per image, no sprite sheet, no layout, no extra weapon, no muzzle flash, no blur, no FX, no text, no border, no watermark. Preserve every design feature; create the new leg articulation rather than deforming or mirroring the old pose.

prompts.correction_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target image 1: James walking with his near-camera leg forward. Image 2: original character-design reference.
Required correction: create the OPPOSITE stride by redrawing the legs ONLY. Keep head, chest, arms, pistol, costume and right-facing direction exactly as image 1. This new frame MUST have the foreground / nearer leg trailing to SCREEN LEFT, and the background / farther leg stepping to SCREEN RIGHT. Do NOT return the same foreground-leg-forward pose.
Anatomy and overlap: from the pelvis, draw the NEAR thigh sloping down-left, its knee LEFT of the pelvis, then its shin descending toward the left rear shoe. This foreground thigh must visibly cover the root of the FAR thigh at the pelvis. The FAR thigh emerges from BEHIND that foreground thigh and slopes down-right into the leading knee and planted leading shoe. The near/rear shoe has the heel raised and its toe at ground. The far/front shoe has a heel contact. Foreground trouser outer seam must be on the LEFT rear leg; the visible right/front leg is the far leg. Keep two anatomically correct legs only. No mirrored upper body, no duplicate limbs, no extra gun.
Maintain same 1280 x 1280 transparent RGBA canvas, same overall sprite size with head near y70 and ground/lowest sole about y1175, same character center and crisp painted arcade style. True alpha zero outside character, no floor, shadows, background, text, FX or layout. One individual full-body pose.
prompts.correction_reason: Initial contact B repeated the near-leg-forward support; replaced with a visibly opposite leg overlap.

validation.alpha_bbox_note: The native image alpha includes faint pixels beyond the visible silhouette. Ground and visible bounds use alpha > 127; do not infer the foot line from alpha > 0.
validation.pivot_note: Suggested x is half the native canvas width; y is the last pixel in the alpha > 127 silhouette. Runtime should apply per-frame alignment against the existing guard.

limitations: These are two walking contact drawings per fighter. They are not a complete fluid walk cycle; passing, up/down and additional transition frames remain to be produced.
Reference fidelity is to the project guard sprite. The new poses are adapted drawings; strict 1:1 correspondence to the original 3D game animation has not been established.
Some face, fabric and shading details vary between generated frames despite the preserved design.
Native outputs measure 1254 x 1254, not the requested 1024 x 1024. Runtime alignment/scaling must handle their measured dimensions and per-frame foot lines.
Code, runtime bindings and shared catalogues are outside this subtask and have not been changed.
